rv.q: This is the best British comedy since One Man, Two Guvnors and deserves equal success.
Moments of sheer stage poetry are mixed with effervescent fun.
This is a play that stands on its own two feet as a heady celebration of the act of theatre.
Like many such beverages, this show is moderately fizzy and leaves a slightly synthetic aftertaste.
It’s funny, romantic and thrilling, dripping with beautiful costumes adorning a huge cast on a simple but stylish set that can be manipulated and lit to create plenty of breathtaking moments.
As Tom Bateman’s unquenchably dynamic Shakespeare reasserts himself, you realize that while the show is hardly newfangled, it’s a big-hearted hit.

cn.t: Critics praise this stage adaptation as a delightfully funny love letter to theatre that finds its true home on the boards, with Lee Hall's witty script and spirited performances generating warmth and genuine emotion.
